items.q: Core diagnostic feature separating delirium from dementia at presentation is what?
o: Impaired attention with acute fluctuating course
items.exp: Delirium begins abruptly with inattention and fluctuation over hours days; dementia creeps over years with attention spared early. Both can coexist, baseline collateral decides acuity.
items.kp: Cannot attend, changes by hour: delirium.

items.q: Which delirium subtype is most commonly missed and has poor prognosis?
items.exp: Quiet drowsy withdrawn hypoactive patients are labelled depressed or tired, delaying cause treatment; mixed is commonest overall in some series but hypoactive is the missed lethal one.
r: Incorrect. Agitation gets noticed and treated.
items.kp: The quiet confused patient is the emergency.

items.q: First line management of delirium on a medical ward is what?
o: Find and treat causes plus multicomponent non drug bundle
items.exp: Cause treatment (infection, fluids, drug stops) with orientation, hydration, mobilisation, sleep and sensory aids is therapy; antipsychotics reserve for severe distress danger, sedation and restraint worsen outcomes.
r: Incorrect. Routine antipsychotics do not shorten delirium.
Correct. Causes plus HELP bundle first.
Incorrect. Benzodiazepines worsen non withdrawal delirium.
items.kp: Treat the cause, free the patient.

items.q: Delirium in Parkinson or Lewy body dementia needing drug for dangerous agitation requires which caution?
o: Severe neuroleptic sensitivity risk; avoid typicals, specialist low dose atypical choices
items.exp: Dopamine blockade can cause life threatening sensitivity reactions in Lewy body disease; management maximises non drug measures, reviews dopaminergic and anticholinergic loads, and uses specialist guided low dose quetiapine or clozapine class options if unavoidable.
r: Incorrect. Typicals are most dangerous here.
Incorrect. Sedation worsens falls and confusion.

items.q: Benzodiazepines in delirium are treatment rather than poison in which scenario?
items.exp: Withdrawal delirium is GABA deficit state where benzodiazepines are definitive; most other delirium worsens with them. Anticholinergic delirium instead needs culprit removal and supportive care.
r: Incorrect. Stop anticholinergics, do not sedate deeper.
items.kp: Only withdrawal delirium drinks benzodiazepines safely.

items.q: CAM assessment requires which mandatory pair?
o: Acute fluctuating course plus inattention, plus disorganised thinking or altered level
items.exp: Confusion Assessment Method algorithm: feature 1 acute fluctuation AND feature 2 inattention, plus either disorganised thinking or altered consciousness. Memory testing alone misses delirium.
r: Incorrect. Those are dementia or psychosis clues.
Correct. Fluctuation plus inattention plus one more.
Incorrect. Fever is cause clue, not criterion.
items.kp: Fluctuates and cannot attend: CAM positive path.

items.q: Most common drug culprits precipitating delirium in elderly include which classes?
o: Anticholinergics, opioids, benzodiazepines and polypharmacy generally
items.exp: Anticholinergic burden, sedatives and opioids on vulnerable brains precipitate delirium; medication review stopping or reducing culprits is first intervention alongside infection and metabolic search.
r: Incorrect. Topicals minimal systemic delirium risk.
items.kp: Review the drug chart before scanning the brain.

items.q: Delirium that persists unexplained for weeks should prompt consideration of which hidden cause among others?
o: Non convulsive seizures, subdural, autoimmune encephalitis re workup
items.exp: Persistent delirium is not a diagnosis to accept: occult infection, chronic subdural, autoimmune or metabolic disease and non convulsive status (EEG) need renewed hunt with neurology input.
r: Correct. Re hunt hidden causes including EEG.
Incorrect. Ageing never fluctuates like this.
Incorrect. Follow up cognition is mandatory.
items.kp: Still delirious at week three: hunt again deeper.

items.q: Delirium prevention bundle proven to cut hospital incidence includes what?
o: Orientation, hydration, early mobilisation, sleep protocol, vision and hearing aids
items.exp: Hospital Elder Life Program style multicomponent care prevents about a third of delirium; prophylactic antipsychotics lack prevention evidence and add harm.
r: Incorrect. Drugs do not prevent delirium.
Incorrect. Immobility and catheters provoke it.
items.kp: Walk, water, glasses, sleep: delirium prevention.

items.q: After delirium resolves, patients carry increased long term risk of what, needing follow up?
o: Dementia and mortality, with cognitive recovery sometimes months
items.exp: Delirium accelerates cognitive decline and predicts dementia diagnosis and death; families should expect slow recovery and clinics recheck cognition, function and mood after discharge.
r: Correct. Dementia and mortality risk rise.
Incorrect. Mood risk is depression more than mania.
items.kp: Surviving delirium still endangers the brain.
